messages:
maya: Quick sync — proposing an "Efficiency Adviser" alpha gating for our inference guidance work. Goal: ship a narrow slice that gives per-route batching/caching/quant recs + eval-triggered alerts for regressions. Short thread to align acceptance and rollout plan.

oleg: +1. Need to be laser on scope. Can we define the narrow slice as: 1) web chat routes, 2) 1M tokens/day, 3) p99 latency budget 300ms?

sam: I like narrowing by route. Mobile native apps will have different constraints so exclude for alpha. Also call out model families (LLaMA2-13B and Redmond-v1) so ops can precompute profiles.

maya: Agreed. Proposal for alpha acceptance (draft):
```
- Supported routes: /v1/chat (web only)
- Models: LLaMA2-13B, redmond-v1 (server-side variants)
- Recommendations: batching window suggestion, prefix-KV cache hint, quantization level suggestion (int8 / int4 fallback)
- Eval-trigger rules: alert if top-1 response quality drops >5% on seeded prompt set OR hallucination rate increases >3% over baseline
- Telemetry: per-route token cost delta, p50/p95/p99 latency, recommendation adoption rate
- Rollout: gradual canary -> 10% -> 50% -> global; auto-fallback to baseline model if error rate >2% for 5m
```

gina: That looks solid. A few questions: how do we measure "recommendation adoption rate"? Is it ops applying config or customers overriding? We should instrument both.

oleg: Implementation nit: batching window suggestion should be expressed as a percentile-driven value (e.g., 95th request-spacing) not a fixed ms. Otherwise it won't generalize across traffic shapes.

maya: Good catch. Change to "suggested batching window = p95 inter-arrival for route, with recommended max 50ms for web chat". Also add a flag to surface "safe-to-quantize" with confidence score.

sam: On eval-triggered alerts: we need a small seeded prompt set (~200 prompts) and lightweight automatic scoring (BLEU/ROUGE + heuristics for hallucination). If we make it too heavy we won't run it often enough.

gina: Ops ask: include a manual "pause recommendations" button in Console for initial alpha so customers can opt out of auto-applied recs. Also require audit log entry on any auto-change.

maya: Rollout gating: accept alpha if the following pass for 72h on canary traffic: adoption rate > 10% (customers applied recs or auto-applied), no quality regression >2% on seeded set, stability errors <1%. If fail, auto-rollback and postmortem.

oleg: Perf checklist for eng-runtime: KV cache check, async batching support per route, quant fallbacks present, metrics export for p99 latency per model variant. Can we mark owners? I can own batching infra changes.

sam: I'll own seeded-eval harness and scoring. Gina, can you own Console UI for the pause/audit bits?

gina: Yep. ETA for alpha UI mock: EOD Fri.

maya: Owners + rough dates:
- Batching infra (oleg): PR by Tue next week
- Eval harness (sam): prototype by Wed next week
- Console pause/audit (gina): mock Fri, implementation in 2 sprints
- Telemetry/metrics (ops): baseline export + adoption metric in 1 sprint

maya: Final questions: do we want to auto-apply recommendations in alpha or keep them read-only? My bias: auto-apply for internal teams + opt-in for customers.

oleg: Prefer read-only initially to validate correctness, but we can auto-apply for internal Redwood test tenants. Safer.

sam: Read-only for customers + auto-apply internal. We can flip after stability window.

gina: Agree. Also add a short in-console explainer: "what this recommendation changes" and link to detailed docs.

deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: canary chart created for route /v1/chat. Notify #eng-releases when ready. :rocket:

maya: Awesome. I'll convert this thread into a short PR with acceptance checklist and ownership. If no objections by EOD, I'll file the RFC and schedule kick-off. :+1:
